To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mice deficient for the ribosomal S6 kinase genes, S6K 1 and S6 K2, exhibit perinatal lethally and rapamycin-sensitive 5′- terminal oligopyrimidine mRNA translation.

the S6 kinases 1 and 2 are required for full activation of 40S protein synthesis initiation factor eIF4B in response to growth factors and that the MAPK-dependent S6 kinase p90rsk can partially compensate for the lack of S6 kinase activity.

(1) S6K1-/- and S6K1 -/-/S6K -/- mice are smaller than wild-type animals, (2) S6K2-/- mice are larger than wild-type animals but have a reduced viability, and (3) S6Ks are not required for the translation of 50S ribosomal protein L7A, 60S ribosomal protein P0, and elongation factor 1α mRNAs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of S6 kinases in the regulation of protein synthesis and cell growth.
the role of S6Ks in mammalian development and physiology and provides a genetic model to study S6K1- and S6K1-independent signaling pathways.
the role of S6Ks in the regulation of cell growth and proliferation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
S6K1 is essential for animal viability, whereas S6 kinase 2 is not.
S6K1 is essential for viability, S6K2 is dispensable for viability, and both S6K1and S6K2are required for normal S6 phosphorylation and 5′- terminal oligopyrimidine mRNA translation.
S6K1 is the major S6K, and S6k2 is the minor S6K, but both are required for full activation of S6.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S6K1 is the primary S6K in vivo and S6K1/S6K2 double knockout is lethal.

the S6Ks are not absolutely required for the proliferative responses mediated by mitogens, but rather, they are important for the maintenance of viability and for the proper development of the embryo.
the absence of SSK1 or SSK2 in mice results in reduced viability and a reduction in S6 kinase activity, and that both SSK1 and SSK2 are required for full activity of this kinase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the S6K1/S6K2 double knockout mice die in utero, and the reason is that they have a defect in translation of mRNAs that are required for cell survival.
the absence of both S6Ks is incompatible with life, but the absence of either S6K1, S6K2 or both S6K1/S6K2 is compatible with life.

the S6K1/2 kinases are not required for cell cycle progression or 5′-TOP mRNA translation, and the S6K pathway is not the only route to S6 phosphorylation, which may occur through other MAPK-dependent kinases.
